title: POC scoping: Solaris - open model shortlist
next_steps: Maya to send POC SOW and pricing for a 6-week pilot by 2027-08-19
Eli to produce model shortlist with perf/quality tradeoffs and estimated infra by 2027-08-20
Customer (Ava) to share 500 sample prompts + 2k historical queries and desired success criteria by 2027-08-19
Schedule 24-hour benchmark run across en/es and domain prompts (target week of 2027-08-23)
action_items: Eli Navarro: deliver model shortlist + expected latency/cost estimates; due 2027-08-20
Maya Patel: send SOW, pricing, and SOC2 pack; due 2027-08-19
Ava Chen: provide sample dataset (CSV) and define pass/fail metrics (accuracy/ROUGE/hallucination tolerances); due 2027-08-19
Samir Rao: confirm network constraints and whether VPC/private deploy needed; due 2027-08-20
meeting_header: Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Eli Navarro (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Solaris), Samir Rao (Solaris), Ava Chen (Solaris)
summary: POC scoping call to define success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan and shortlist open models for a 6-week pilot. Customer prioritized accuracy on medical triage/notes, bilingual support (EN/ES), and strict data residency with potential VPC. Discussed tradeoffs between larger LLMs vs smaller quantized models and proposed benchmark plan (24-hour perf run + quality evals).
topics: Success criteria: accuracy, hallucination rate, latency SLOs
Workload sizing: expected QPS, concurrency, burst patterns
Model shortlist: open-model candidates and tradeoffs (quality, cost, multilingual)
Deployment constraints: dedicated vs private/VPC, KMS encryption, audit/logging
transcript: [00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll run about 45 minutes then leave time for next steps, Eli and I are from Redwood.

[00:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Great, thanks. We just want to make sure we scope the POC so we can validate model selection and infra — we have sensitive patient-ish data, so residency and KMS are important.
[00:25] Eli Navarro: Absolutely. Quick high level: goal today is success criteria, workload, shortlist open models, benchmark plan, and timeline. We'll propose 6-week pilot usually — is that ok?
[00:36] Samir Rao: 6 weeks sounds fine. We're most worried about hallucinations in clinical triage and Spanish support — about 30% of our users are Spanish-first.

[00:48] Ava Chen: I'll add that latency matters for triage — we target p95 < 800ms for user-facing flows, batch jobs can be higher. Also cost is a factor; we can't spin up huge GPUs for long durations.

[01:05] Eli Navarro: Good notes — so success criteria from Redwood perspective and confirm from Solaris: accuracy on intent extraction > X, hallucination rate under Y, bilingual support EN/ES, p95 latency target 800ms for interactive. Does that capture it?
[01:20] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Yes, and add a post-edit rate target — we want less than 5% manual correction for generated summaries in the clinical notes use-case.
[01:30] Maya Patel: Perfect. On workload sizing — Samir, what's your expected concurrency/QPS for the pilot?

[01:39] Samir Rao: For the pilot initial traffic will be small — around 20 concurrent users, peaks to 50. In production we expect 200-300 concurrent during daytime across regions. For benchmarking though, we want to simulate 500 QPS to see headroom.

[01:56] Eli Navarro: Great — for the 24-hour benchmark we'll scale to 500 QPS synthetic traffic with realistic prompt distribution. We'll test multi-lingual splits 70% EN / 30% ES and domain prompts: triage, notes summarization, question-answering.
[02:10] Ava Chen: For dataset I'll provide 500 sample prompts + 2k anonymized historical queries; can Redwood use that for quality evals?
[02:18] Maya Patel: Yes, that's exactly what we need. We'll run automated metrics (exact match / F1 where applicable, ROUGE for summaries) and human evals for hallucination sampling.
[02:30] Dr. Lena Ortiz: On model shortlist — what do you recommend for open models that balance cost and medical quality?

[02:38] Eli Navarro: We're thinking a 3-tier shortlist: (1) smaller quantized models for throughput/cost — e.g., Mistral 7B/8B quantized to 4-bit; (2) mid-size models like Falcon-40B or Llama 2-Chat 70B in 8-bit or 4-bit depending on infra; (3) larger instruction-tuned or customized variants if we need higher quality — e.g., Llama 3 variants or fine-tuned Llama-2-Chat derivatives. Each has tradeoffs in hallucination and multilingual tokenization.
[03:00] Samir Rao: Quick clarification — we'll need Spanish performance. Which of these has better ES out-of-box?

[03:07] Eli Navarro: Historically Mistral family and Llama variants have decent multilingual capacity when instruction-tuned, Falcon sometimes lags on ES for medical domain. We can also run lightweight domain fine-tuning or LoRA on top. For pilot we usually test zero-shot then one-shot then LoRA to measure gains.
[03:26] Ava Chen: How about quantization impact on hallucination and Spanish tokenization? We've seen some quality drop when we go to 4-bit for our NER tasks.

[03:34] Eli Navarro: Good point — quantization can slightly degrade output fidelity, more noticeable on sensitive domain tasks. We'll include quality checks at each quantization level (fp16, 8-bit, 4-bit) in the benchmark. Also consider prefix/KV cache to keep latency low for long context use-cases.
[03:49] Maya Patel: Deployment options given your residency requirement — do you prefer Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved capacity) or Private (VPC/on-prem)?
[03:57] Samir Rao: Preference is a VPC/private control plane if possible due to compliance. We can discuss a dedicated pool if private is too heavy for the pilot.
[04:05] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Yes we need KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO — SOC2 proof would help.

[04:12] Maya Patel: We'll attach SOC2 and SSO/SAML docs. For the pilot we can do a Private deployment in your VPC — it takes a bit more ops work but meets residency/KMS needs. Alternatively, Redwood Dedicated with encrypted-at-rest and dedicated GPU pools is quicker if VPC is delayed.
[04:30] Ava Chen: Network team note: we have strict egress rules — can the benchmark be run in our environment?

[04:36] Eli Navarro: Yes, we can run the benchmark inside your VPC or in our dedicated environment with synthetic data. For end-to-end perf and networking you should run the 24-hour benchmark inside your infra.
[04:46] Samir Rao: Great. Let's talk metrics for perf: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, GPU utilization. Also need memory footprint for different model sizes.

[04:58] Eli Navarro: We'll collect p50/p95, cold vs warm latencies, throughput per GPU, and estimated $/1M tokens using both on-demand and reserved pricing. We'll report memory usage and expected concurrency per GPU with recommended batch sizes.
[05:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Benchmarks — what's a realistic timeline?

[05:16] Maya Patel: If we get sample data and SOW signed this week, Redwood can run initial zero-shot quality and perf runs within 7 days, then a full 24-hour benchmark the week after. So kickoff 8/23, initial results by 8/30, full 24-hour by 9/6, then LoRA/fine-tune runs and final evaluation by the end of the 6-week pilot.

[05:31] Ava Chen: That timeline works. For acceptance criteria, we'll define gold-standard outputs for 200 prompts and require >= 92% on targeted extraction tasks and <5% hallucination on sampled outputs.
[05:43] Eli Navarro: Sounds good. We'll make the acceptance criteria explicit in the SOW. On the shortlist we propose to test the following models during the initial runs:
[05:52] Eli Navarro: - Mistral-7B-instruct (quantized 4-bit for throughput) — good cost profile, strong general instruction-following, often good multilingual when tuned,
[06:03] Eli Navarro: - Falcon-40B/Instruct — mid-size, good instruction tuning but sometimes needs extra domain fine-tuning for medical specifics,
[06:13] Eli Navarro: - Llama-2-Chat 70B — strong few-shot generalization, better hallucination handling when instruction-tuned; heavier memory footprint,
[06:24] Eli Navarro: - MPT-30B (or derivative) — pragmatic tradeoff between cost and quality for summarization tasks,
[06:32] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Any concerns with licensing for these open models? We need commercial-use permissive licenses.

[06:38] Maya Patel: We'll check licensing for each candidate; Redwood maintains a model catalog and will flag any restrictive licenses. Generally Mistral/Falcon/Llama variants are fine for commercial usage but we will double-check.
[06:50] Samir Rao: How do you measure hallucination? Manual sampling or automated detection?

[06:55] Eli Navarro: Both. We'll run automated hallucination detectors (e.g., entailment-based checks, citation mismatch heuristics) and human spot-checks for clinical risky outputs. We'll include a small human review panel for the pilot.
[07:08] Ava Chen: On hardware — what GPUs do you recommend for the 40B/70B runs? H100? A100?

[07:15] Eli Navarro: For 40B, A100 80GB or H100 are fine; 70B is best on H100 80GB for memory and perf. For cheaper runs we can test 4-bit quantized on A100 with nvlink. We'll include cost delta in the report.
[07:29] Maya Patel: We'll also surface recommendations like batch sizes, batching windows, and KV cache settings to hit latency targets while maximizing throughput.
[07:38] Dr. Lena Ortiz: If we find Falcon has lower Spanish accuracy, would you recommend LoRA vs full fine-tune?
[07:44] Eli Navarro: LoRA usually gives 80-95% of full fine-tune gains at a fraction of cost/time — for pilot we typically try LoRA first on a curated 5-10k example set.
[07:55] Samir Rao: Security checklist — SSO, SAML, KMS, audit logs, data retention controls. We need a doc with the controls and how Redwood meets them.
[08:03] Maya Patel: We'll attach the security pack (SOC2, ISO summary, SSO steps, KMS integration guide). We'll also include data retention config options for the POC.
[08:12] Ava Chen: Anything about caching and privacy? If we cache prefixes, we need to ensure PHI isn't stored longer than policy allows.
[08:19] Eli Navarro: Cache can be configured per-route — we can disable persistent caching for routes carrying PHI and use ephemeral KV cache with TTL to ensure compliance.
[08:31] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Good. Back to benchmarks — what metrics do you provide for summarization quality? ROUGE, BLEU, ROUGE-L? Also clinical-specific metrics?

[08:39] Eli Navarro: We'll provide ROUGE/ROUGE-L for summaries, F1/Exact match for extraction, and we can run clinical-entity overlap metrics (you might have an ontology we can align with). We'll do human scoring for clinical correctness.

[08:53] Maya Patel: Let's outline the POC phases for clarity: Phase 0: Kickoff & data exchange; Phase 1: zero-shot baseline + perf on small infra; Phase 2: 24-hour benchmark and quantization experiments; Phase 3: LoRA/fine-tune experiments; Phase 4: acceptance & ops handoff.
[09:08] Samir Rao: That sequencing looks good. For acceptance we'll run the 200 gold prompts you mentioned; if model passes we move to production pilot sizing.
[09:16] Ava Chen: Onprod requirements — if we go to private deployment later, we need an operator runbook and SLO dashboard.
[09:22] Maya Patel: Redwood Console provides per-route token breakdowns, p95/p99, model-level dashboards, and rollouts. We'll include the runbook as part of the handoff.
[09:32] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Any red flags from Redwood side?
[09:35] Eli Navarro: Only that we need the sample dataset and network constraints early. Also license checks on exact model variant need to be confirmed. Nothing else blocking.

[09:44] Maya Patel: Ok quick recap: deliverables and owners — Eli: model shortlist + perf/cost estimates; Maya: SOW + security pack; Ava: sample data + acceptance metrics; Samir: confirm network/VPC preference. We'll plan kickoff 8/23 and run bench week of 8/30.
[09:58] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Thanks all. One more quick question: for multi-lingual QA, should we consider separate fine-tuned models per language?

[10:05] Eli Navarro: In many cases a single multilingual model suffices if tuned with bilingual data. But if Spanish performance remains weak, we can evaluate language-specific LoRAs or a two-model routing policy where EN->model A and ES->model B. We'll include routing cost in the report.
[10:20] Ava Chen: Good — please include routing policy cost and complexity in the deliverable.
[10:25] Maya Patel: Will do. Anything else before we close?
[10:29] Samir Rao: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[10:32] Maya Patel: Great, we'll send SOW and scheduling invite. Talk soon!
